summary: The study describes the thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of continuous and highly conducting gold thin films using Me2Au(S2CNEt2) as the gold precursor and ozone (O3) as the co-reactant. The process was evaluated at temperatures ranging from 120 to 250 °C, with optimal self-limiting growth observed at 180 °C. The deposited films were uniform, polycrystalline, and conductive, with resistivity values as low as 4–16 µΩ·cm for 40 nm thick films. The compound Me2Au(S2CNEt2) showed good thermal stability and volatility, making it suitable for ALD.
evidence: ABSTRACT: Five Au(III) compounds were synthesized and evaluated for atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Au thin films. One of the compounds, Me2Au(S2CNEt2), showed optimal thermal characteristics being volatile and thermally stable. In the growth experiments this compound was applied with O3 at temperatures 120 – 250 °C. Self-limiting growth was confirmed at 180 °C with a rate of 0.9 Å/cycle. The deposited Au thin films were uniform, polycrystalline, continuous and conductive. Typical resistivity values of 40 nm thick films were 4 – 16 µΩ·cm which are low for chemically deposited thin films.
